messages:
release_manager: Heads up — while cleaning up the release notes I spotted a deploy JWT for user-service embedded in the public notes: `eyJhbGci...<redacted>`.
sec_oncall: Ack. Can you paste the notes link and a short context? Is this a long-lived token or a CI ephemeral?
release_manager: Link: https://releases.redwood.ai/2026-03-19/user-service. It looks like the token was copied into the notes by mistake. I only saw the truncated value, not the full secret. No clue on TTL.
maria: Thanks. I'll run a quick scan against secrets index and CI artifacts. @devops_bot can you surface the token metadata if it exists in the key registry?
devops_bot: secret-scan v2: matched hash for token fragment "eyJhbGci" in artifact release-notes-2026-03-19.txt. Possible match id: leak-20260319-01. No exact key id available from the fragment.
ian: I'm checking the deploy agent registry. If this is a deploy JWT it may be issued by deploy-svc and live in the KMS alias `projects/redwood/keys/deploy-jwt-user`. Querying now.
sophia: Flagging this as P1 exposure until we know TTL/usage. If the token was in public notes, assume compromise and rotate + revoke immediately. Also start customer-impact check for any API calls authenticated with that token.
sec_oncall: Action list:
1) Revoke candidate key(s) immediately (manual revoke in key registry).
2) Rotate any deploy credentials referenced by CI/CD and update KMS aliases.
3) Run audit query for token usage and IPs.
4) Notify infra and release teams and create an incident record.

I'll kick off 1 and 4 now. @maria @ian pick 2 and 3.
maria: Running gitleaks/trufflehog over the release notes, build artifacts, and S3 release bucket. Command: 
```
trufflehog filesystem --path ./release-artifacts/2026-03-19 --rules ./rules.yaml --entropy true
```
I'll post results.
ian: Found a matching key id in the registry: deploy-jwt-user-78f4. TTL: 30 days, created 2026-03-01. Marking for immediate revoke. Revoking via internal API:
```
POST https://kms.internal.redwood/v1/keys/deploy-jwt-user-78f4/revoke
Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN
```
Response: 200 OK — key state: revoked.
sophia: Great. maria please attach any external access logs. I'm running the audit query to check usage from 2026-03-01 -> now:
```
SELECT timestamp, src_ip, endpoint, user_agent FROM audit.logs WHERE auth_token_id = 'deploy-jwt-user-78f4' ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 1000;
```
Preliminary: 2 runs from our CI IPs, no external src_ip yet. Continuing.
release_manager: I've removed the token snippet from the public notes and created a sanitized version. Notifying the release channel. @sec_oncall filed INC-2026-0319-01 and assigned owners.
sec_oncall: Confirming revoke succeeded. Next: rotate the deploy agent to use a new key and update KMS alias. ia n/maria can you push the new secret to KMS and update the deploy config? Use the short-lived service tokens pattern.
ian: New key created: deploy-jwt-user-9b2c. TTL 7d, rotation scheduled daily for deploy agents. Updated deploy-svc config to fetch alias `projects/redwood/keys/deploy-jwt-user` from KMS. Pushed patch to infra repo: PR #982. CI is green.
maria: Scanned artifacts again — no remaining matches. Report: leak-20260319-01 resolved; artifacts cleaned and invalidated in S3. gitleaks output attached: zero new findings.
sophia: Customer impact check complete: no requests from non-internal IPs; no anomalous API calls attributed to that token. Recommend: internal postmortem, update release checklist to prevent copy/paste into notes, add automated pre-publish secret scan.
sec_oncall: Agreed. Post-incident actions:
- Mandatory pre-publish secret-scan for release notes (owner: release_manager)
- Update CI to pull keys from KMS only (owner: ian)
- Create alert for public helm/changelogs containing secrets (owner: maria)
- Postmortem doc in #postmortems in 48h (owner: sec_oncall)

I'll close INC-2026-0319-01 when PR #982 is merged and KMS alias verified.
release_manager: PR merged, release notes sanitized, communications sent to release channel and product. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
sec_oncall: Closing thread — moving to postmortem drafting. If you touched any artifacts, please add a short timeline to the incident doc.
